title: 'I stayed in America's most haunted room and was shaken awake by an apparition'
excerpt: I woke up at least three times during my one-night stay, and it wasn't natural. It felt like a jolt had gone through my body, and my vision was a bit blurry. I believe I saw her apparition kneeling on my side of the bed, staring a few inches from my face
content:
Mataeo Smith

Sat, October 31, 2026 at 2:00 PM UTC

The ominous halls of the Congress Plaza Hotel in Chicago are like being in your own thriller, as I found myself opening doors I would normally tell the protagonist not to.

But I couldn't help it. Maybe it was because I knew I would inevitably encounter an apparition known to shake awake inhabitants of room 441, believed to be America's most haunted hotel room. Nobody knows who the woman is or why she peeks through the bathroom shower curtain, but she's definitely there and seems intent on disturbing visitors' sleep before retiring to the spacious closet near the front door.

I woke up at least three times during my one-night stay, and it wasn't natural. It felt like a jolt had gone through my body, and my vision was a bit blurry. I believe I saw her apparition kneeling on my side of the bed, staring a few inches from my face. The creepy paranormal activity largely stopped there, but it was profound.

I can't say that I saw a full-blown ghost, but there was a moment when the marble tiles on the wall appaeared to shift into a humanoid face as I washed my hand - a common occurrence when in the presence of an apparition.

"Everyone says that a black figure comes out of the washroom late at night while they're watching TV, and it stops at the foot of the bed and just stands there. Then it moves on and goes toward the closet. If the closet is closed, it opens it up, walks in there, and closes it behind it," security guard Johnny D., 62, told The Mirror US.

"Next thing you know, people are calling us. Once we get up there, it takes off," he added.

According to local legend, the 133-year-old hotel is haunted by at least three spirits.

One boy died tragically in 1939 after his mother allegedly tossed him out of the window on the 12th story to avoid the Nazis. According to Johnny D, his body was never found.

Although there is no concrete proof linking the infamous mobster Al Capone to the historic hotel, there are rumors that his ghost haunts the eighth floor and paces the hallway.

And most notably, the woman in room 441, where I stayed. Surprisingly, no one knows for sure who this spirit belonged to, but she is one of the most active ghosts in the entire building. People who’ve stayed in the room say she loves to play with the bathroom lights, shake inhabitants awake, and rip the covers off them as they sleep.

"You see them on TV; you see them in a movie, but I'm telling you it ain't nothing until you see it real life," Johnny D said, adding that he saw the ghost of the boy killed by his mom sitting in the corner of one room.

I survived the night, but wish it was a bit more eventful. I love the paranormal and have seen ghosts a handful of times in my own home. The black-haired woman didn't feel the need to bother me any more than she already had, but maybe I'll return next year for another crack at it.
